chapter: After the Army: JATP, clubs and first Europe trips
title: His own seven-piece band in the late 1940s
summary: Clayton describes his small band's tours, personnel including Skip Hall, George Duvivier and Skinny Brown.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Where did you meet, run into him then, in the Army?
Well, no. He, you see, I also during those years when I was working with Joe Bushkin, I had my own band and he was one of the members of the band.
Oh, we made tours down to Virginia. We made Washington D.C. We played the Ioward, we played Apollo.
Seven. George Jerry Duvivier was my bass player. Joe Benjamin, after George Duvivier, Joe Benjamin came. Len Davis was my alto and Skip, you know Skip Hall?
Yes. He was my piano. We had a nice, that was a nice band too.

Oh, I've forgotten that little boy's name, he was kind of a young kid, I've forgotten his name now. He was Eli Robinson's cousin. And Step was the second trumpet player. In other words, we had three brass and two, two, I must have had about an eight-piece band. Skinny Brown was on tenor sax. He was one of the Savoy Sultans. You remember that old Savoy Sultan, he had played with Pat Jenkins.
They had a good swinging band. But he was a tenor player and Len Davis was the alto player and me and Step and Dickie Harris .....
